canonical.behaviour: Revision of offer #3 with agreement 4, after the owner's answers Q9 to Q11; everything else stays as approved. (1) The labeler's local backend is http://<local backend name>, the real server's name kept on this PC by the hosts file. The guard pins it: Chromium resolves that name to 127.0.0.1 itself, and a run refuses to start unless Node also resolves it to this machine. verify-app's guard gains this pin as a general setting, with tests. <local backend name> leaves the labeler's blocked list; the other production hosts stay blocked. (2) Playwright is installed in the labeler with npm install and npx playwright install chromium; other packages may change because the lockfile is older. (3) The local database is a staging copy with test data only, so runs use a test account in it as it is. (4) T7 adds the Dashboard screen. Phase 1 of checking things in the real app, as agreed in agreement 3. workflow-axa gets two new skills written as its own text from pstack (MIT, credited in VENDORED-SKILLS.md, not installed): verify-app, which writes and maintains an app's verify skill and feature map, with a guide for adding screens and new jobs and a browser-guard template; and reproduce-bug, the bug job, which reproduces a bug report twice in the running app and checks a known fix, with the outcomes Reproduced, Could not reproduce, Blocked, Fix confirmed and Fix not confirmed. Both are registered and tested in the package. Then, in the the test app labeler, verify-app writes .claude/skills/verify-labeler/ with a map of My labels; it must pass the 9-step setup check and the guard checks, where production is refused and other hosts are blocked. The first test checks the filter-dot fix 502db1f, the eval checks two more fixed bugs, and a second screen is added by following only the guide. One assumption changed: the candidate skills are read by path from D:\workflow-axa in the labeler session, instead of through tools/stage_candidate.py, which only builds a separate sandbox repository (E6).
